privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: This app is built to collect as little data about you as possible.
privacy.whatWeUseBody: Your location (only in your browser, to fetch the forecast) and chosen language are stored locally on your device. If you enable aurora alerts, we store your push subscription and a coarse location to send the alert.
privacy.whatWeDontBody: No cross-site tracking and no selling of data. No ads are shown today; if ads are introduced, you will be asked for consent first where the law requires it.
privacy.retentionBody: You can turn off alerts at any time, which deletes your subscription.
privacy.analyticsBody: We count visits on our own server in aggregate — without cookies and without tracking you across sites — so there is no consent banner to click.

hero.title: Get notified the day before your best chance to see the northern lights
hero.lead: We watch the aurora forecast (Kp from NOAA) and MET Norway's cloud forecast for your place. When the next night looks good, you hear about it the afternoon before – so you have time to plan.
hero.step2: Choose how: browser, e-mail or app
hero.step3: Get a heads-up the afternoon before a good night
hero.free: Free. At most one alert per night. Unsubscribe in one click.

alerts.title: Aurora alerts
alerts.pickPlace: Pick a place above first – search, tap the map or use your location.
alerts.channels: How do you want to be alerted?
alerts.nowOption: Also a “happening now” alert when it's dark, clear and active (at most one per night, not 02–06)
alerts.highOnly: Only when the chance is high
alerts.nightsNote: The alert goes out the afternoon before a night with a good or high chance.
alerts.rule: How it works: each night gets a chance (low, good, high) from how many dark hours have a Kp high enough for your latitude and under 40% cloud. If the next night is good or high, we send one alert between 15:00 and 21:00 the day before.
